Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

BUILD: revenue and retention analytics for the admin panel.

## Read this trap before designing anything
The board asks for "Revenue analytics (MRR / ARR / churn / LTV / CAC)". **Most of those metrics do not apply to this product and computing them would produce confident nonsense.**

Check `lib/stripe.ts` yourself: `CREDIT_PACKS` are `mode: "payment"` one-time purchases. There is no subscription anywhere in the codebase. So:
- **MRR/ARR are undefined.** There is no recurring revenue to annualise. Do not invent one by averaging purchases over months and calling it MRR.
- **Churn is undefined** in the subscription sense. Someone who bought credits and stopped building has not churned; they have credits sitting unused.
- **CAC is uncomputable** — nothing in this codebase records marketing spend or attribution. Do not fabricate it.
- **LTV is computable** but only as realised revenue per user to date, not a projection.

Report what you refused to compute and why. Building the honest subset is the task; building the requested-but-meaningless set would be worse than building nothing.

## What IS genuinely computable — build this
Read `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/credits.ts`, `lib/events.ts` first.
1. **Realised revenue** — from `CreditLedger` rows whose `reason` starts with `stripe:`, converted via `CREDIT_PACKS`, over time. Note the ledger stores credits granted, not dollars; work out the mapping honestly and say where it is approximate.
2. **Cost and margin over time** — `Build.costMicros` vs `Build.creditsCharged * MICROS_PER_CREDIT`. **Important caveat you must surface in the UI:** when `KODELY_ENGINE=sdk`, costs are IMPUTED, not billed — read the header comment in `lib/agent-sdk.ts`. A margin dashboard that presents imputed cost as real money is misleading.
3. **Signup cohorts and retention** — group users by signup week, then show what share of each cohort reached a first build, a first publish, and a purchase, and whether they were still building in later weeks. Use `Event` rows (`lib/events.ts`) and `Build`/`Project` data. **The `Event` table is nearly empty** (tracking is new) — build a real empty state and say so.
4. **Credit liability** — total unspent credits outstanding. That is a genuine obligation: those credits will cost real model spend when used. This is arguably the most useful number on the page and nothing currently shows it.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT: `app/admin/analytics/**`
DO NOT edit anything under lib/, app/api/**, other app/admin/** subtrees (users, sites, flags, feedback, audit and the root page are all owned by other agents right now), app/projects/**, app/dashboard/**, app/settings/**, app/globals.css, prisma/schema.prisma, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.

## Constraints
- `getAdminUser()` from `lib/auth.ts` at the top of every page, `notFound()` if null.
- **No N+1.** Use `groupBy`/`aggregate`/raw SQL with bound parameters. Read `app/admin/users/page.tsx` — it solves this with a single `DISTINCT ON` pass and explains why.
- Match the admin visual idiom: `rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, `tabular-nums`, monochrome. Reuse the funnel-bar pattern from `app/admin/page.tsx` rather than inventing charts.
- No new white-on-brand-gradient text (fails contrast — known accepted issue).
- No new npm dependencies — **no charting library**; simple CSS bars and tables only.
- Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH be clean.** Parallel agents are running — errors in files you did not touch are not yours.
- Local Postgres available read-only; clean up anything you create.

## Report back
Which requested metrics you refused to compute and why, what you built instead, how you handled the imputed-cost caveat, the credit liability figure against real data, and what you verified.

Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

## What is Next.js?

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.

It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.

Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.

## How to use the docs
